knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure classifies the soil and the finish before a method is chosen. Matching the method to both is the core of the lesson.
The worked decision rejects a metal scraper on painted cabinetry and selects a less abrasive authorised alternative. Spot tests need authorisation.
The practice task asks for a written safe sequence and identification of when manufacturer advice is needed. Results alone are not the record.

practicalCriteria: Learner identifies the soil as dry or adhered and chooses the mildest method from a supplied set that removes it.
Learner tests the chosen method on a hidden area of a supplied surface and checks the result after contact and drying time.
Learner records the method, product, contact time and test result, and does not escalate without approval.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Job record with method, product, contact time, test result and any change approved
stopWorkCriteria: Learner uses an abrasive method on a glossy finish without testing
Learner escalates to a stronger method without approval
